papers.title: In Situ Printing of Polylactic Acid/Nanoceramic Filaments for the Repair of Bone Defects Using a Portable 3D Device.
papers.abstract: In situ 3D printing is attractive for the direct repair of bone defects in underdeveloped countries and in emergency situations. So far, the lack of an interesting method to produce filament using FDA-approved biopolymers and nanoceramics combined with a portable strategy limits the use of in situ 3D printing. Herein, we investigated the osseointegration of new nanocomposite filaments based on polylactic acid (PLA), laponite (Lap), and hydroxyapatite (Hap) printed directly at the site of the bone defect in rats using a portable 3D printer. The filaments were produced using a single-screw extruder (L/D = 26), without the addition of solvents that can promote the toxicity of the materials. In vitro performance was evaluated in the cell differentiation process with mesenchymal stem cells (MSC) by an alkaline phosphatase activity test and visualization of mineralization nodules; a cell viability test and total protein dosage were performed to evaluate cytotoxicity. For the in vivo analysis, the PLA/Lap composite filaments with a diameter of 1.75 mm were printed directly into bone defects of Wistar rats using a commercially available portable 3D printer. Based on the in vitro and in vivo results, the in situ 3D printing technique followed by rapid cooling proved to be promising for bone tissue engineering. The absence of fibrous encapsulation and inflammatory processes became a good indicator of effectiveness in terms of biocompatibility parameters and bone tissue formation, and the use of the portable 3D printer showed a significant advantage in the application of this material by in situ printing.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文涉及骨缺损修复中的3D打印技术，但使用FDM而非LPBF，未涉及应力遮挡或疲劳性能。
llm.why_not_core: This paper uses FDM-based extrusion printing, not LPBF, and does not include porous structure design, mechanical testing, or fatigue analysis.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发便携式原位3D打印方法修复骨缺损。
summary_zh.method: 使用单螺杆挤出机制备PLA/纳米陶瓷复合丝材，并通过便携式打印机原位打印。
summary_zh.result: 原位打印后快速冷却促进骨组织形成，无纤维包裹或炎症。
summary_zh.validation: 体外MSC分化与体内大鼠骨缺损模型验证。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a portable in situ 3D printing technique using FDA-approved biopolymers and nanoceramics for direct bone defect repair.
summary_en.method: Nanocomposite filaments of PLA, laponite, and hydroxyapatite were extruded via a single-screw extruder and printed directly into rat bone defects using a portable 3D printer.
summary_en.result: In situ printing followed by rapid cooling promoted bone tissue formation without fibrous encapsulation or inflammation, indicating good biocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: In vitro alkaline phosphatase activity and mineralization assays with MSCs, and in vivo implantation in Wistar rat bone defects.
